limitations: Complete lesson 58 machine transcript read; no comprehensive audiovisual/board verification
All numerical material-property and strength coefficients are invented teaching inputs, not a real-alloy assessment
The formal Fe/Ti/C endmember calculation and the scalar combined-strength example have independent composition assumptions
Pressure model is local; positive responses at one state do not establish wide-range EOS accuracy
Log-viscosity representation/interaction inversion is a stated model, not imported Gibbs interaction parameters or an executed product schema
Strength laws, fixed particle fraction and operation-average examples are deliberately reduced; no complete Seidman implementation or dislocation-population homogenization is claimed
Commercial Al–Sc curves, input file, exact configuration and measured points not independently reproduced
Selected primary sections and versioned documentation only; no full paper/recommendation/literature or SDK verification
counting_method: Whitespace tokens in exact authored article including math and code, excluding reader chrome
